author: The Linux Foundation
description:
Dipesh Rawat, Kubernetes v1.37 Release Lead at CNCF, gives teams a concrete checklist for evaluating new features before enabling them in production clusters.

Full article and transcript: https://tfir.io/kubernetes-upgrade-prep-deprecation-cncf/ 

Skipping pre-upgrade evaluation is the fastest way to introduce instability into a production Kubernetes cluster. Deprecations, incomplete migrations, and premature alpha feature adoption are the most common causes of post-upgrade incidents.

In this exclusive interview with Swapnil Bhartiya, Dipesh Rawat, Kubernetes v1.37 Release Lead at CNCF, walks through exactly what platform teams need to review before turning on any new features from the v1.37 release.

Key Topics Covered:
- How to read the official v1.37 release notes and where deprecation and migration guides live
- How to audit your existing cluster for components affected by upcoming deprecations
- When alpha features are safe to test and how to feed findings back to the community
title: Kubernetes v1.37 Upgrade Prep: What to Check Before Enabling New Features | Dipesh Rawat, CNCF

Off the Laptop, Into Production: An Open Source Stack for AI Agents on Kubernetes - Brian Hammons & Nirmal Mehta, Amazon Web Services

AI agents are fast becoming how modern software gets built. But taking one from prototype to safe, production-grade operation is still genuinely challenging, and how they behave at scale remains largely uncharted. Agents are stochastic, so testing becomes continuous evaluation. They run code nobody wrote, so a shared kernel stops being a boundary you can trust. They decide their own network calls at runtime, so egress is no longer predictable. And they still need what any service needs: source control, CI/CD, observability, memory, and tool access.
